name: HLOOKUP
description: HLOOKUP searches for a value in the first row of a table and returns a value from a specified row in the same column. It is the horizontal counterpart to VLOOKUP.
tldr: Looks up a value across rows (horizontal search).

parameters.name: lookup_value
parameters.description: The value to find in the first row of the table.

parameters.name: table_array
parameters.description: The range containing the data; the first row is searched.

parameters.name: row_index_num
parameters.description: The row number within the table (1-based) from which to return a value.

parameters.name: range_lookup
parameters.description: TRUE for an approximate match (first row sorted ascending), FALSE for an exact match. Defaults to TRUE.

basicExample.result: Value from row 3 of the matched column
basicExample.explanation: HLOOKUP finds "Q2" in row 1, then returns the value in row 3 of that column.

advancedExamples.title: Exact match lookup
advancedExamples.scenario: Product codes across the top row, data beneath
advancedExamples.explanation: With FALSE, only an exact code match returns the row 4 value.

advancedExamples.title: Approximate match (sorted)
advancedExamples.description: Find the bracket containing a score
advancedExamples.explanation: With TRUE it finds the largest threshold not exceeding 85 in the sorted first row.

howItWorks: HLOOKUP scans the first row of table_array for lookup_value. With range_lookup FALSE it requires an exact match; with TRUE it finds the closest value less than or equal to the lookup in an ascending first row, then returns the corresponding value from row_index_num.

howToSteps.name: Prepare the table
howToSteps.text: Put search keys in the first row and data below.

howToSteps.name: Set the row index
howToSteps.text: Count which row (from the top) to return.

howToSteps.name: Choose match type
howToSteps.text: Use FALSE for exact, TRUE for approximate on sorted data.

limitations: Looks only downward within the matched column; it cannot return values from rows above the match row.
Approximate matching (TRUE) requires the first row sorted ascending or results are wrong.
Hard-codes the row position, so inserting rows breaks row_index_num. XLOOKUP avoids this fragility.

commonErrors.cause: lookup_value is not found (exact match) or data is unsorted for approximate match.
commonErrors.fix: Verify the key exists, or sort the first row ascending for TRUE.

commonErrors.cause: row_index_num is greater than the number of rows in table_array.
commonErrors.fix: Reduce row_index_num to a valid row.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: HLOOKUP works the same in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Identical behavior to Excel; XLOOKUP is also available in Sheets.

faq.question: HLOOKUP vs VLOOKUP?
faq.answer: HLOOKUP searches horizontally across the first row; VLOOKUP searches vertically down the first column.

faq.question: Why do I get #N/A?
faq.answer: Usually the key isn't found for an exact match, or the first row isn't sorted for an approximate match.

faq.question: Is there a better alternative?
faq.answer: XLOOKUP (Microsoft 365) is more flexible and avoids the row-index fragility.
